How can there be stability? Does he not look upon me? <gloss>This is a <term>fu</term> <gloss>narrative mode</gloss>.</gloss>


<term>Mào</term> <gloss>to cover/shine upon</gloss>, following the eye radical.
<term>Hū</term> <gloss>exclamation particle</gloss>, read as the reverse of <term>dào</term>.
<term>Bào</term> <gloss>to report/repay</gloss>, read as the reverse.


◯ Sun and Moon, you shine down on the earth below. As for this person, he leaves and does not remain friendly.

How can there be stability? Does he not respond to me? <gloss>This is a <term>fu</term>.</gloss>

◯ Sun and Moon, you rise from the east. As for this person, his virtuous words are not good.

How can there be stability? How can I forget? <gloss>This is a <term>fu</term>.</gloss>

◯ Sun and Moon, in the east you rise. Oh my father, oh my mother, you did not care for me until the end. How can there be stability? You do not report back to me. <gloss>This is a <term>fu</term>. ◯ Zhuang Jiang was not answered by Duke Zhuang, so she called to the Sun and Moon to complain of this, and composed this poem.</gloss>

<gloss>This poem</gloss>
Sun and Moon, four stanzas, each stanza six lines.

<summary>This page contains the poem "Sun and Moon" from the Odes of Bei, in which the speaker, identified as Zhuang Jiang, laments her abandonment by the Duke and her estrangement from her parents, using the celestial bodies as witnesses to her distress.</summary>
<keywords>Sun and Moon, Zhuang Jiang, Duke Zhuang, Odes of Bei, lament, abandonment, filial piety</keywords>
